articles.title: Building Grounded AI Slides with DOM Patches, Geometry Guards, and Headless Chrome
articles.excerpt: Most AI presentation tools make the same architectural mistake: they treat slide creation as a full-document replacement problem. When a user asks an LLM to "make this card look cleaner" or "add a fou…
articles.body: Most AI presentation tools make the same architectural mistake: they treat slide creation as a full-document replacement problem. When a user asks an LLM to "make this card look cleaner" or "add a four-step process", the model typically regenerates the whole slide HTML or returns an un-editable raster image. If you have spent ten minutes tweaking typography, spacing, and brand colours, watching an AI overwrite your entire canvas is infuriating. The second failure mode is layout drift. LLMs have no spatial awareness. When asked to insert three columns or expand an explanation, they happily output HTML that overflows viewport boundaries, clips underneath headers, or pushes footers off the screen.

articles.title: Give your LangChain agent a data tool that says "I can't verify that" instead of guessing
articles.excerpt: Give an agent a database tool and ask it about last quarter's revenue. Most of the time you get a good answer. Sometimes the tool comes back empty, or with something the agent doesn't quite understand…
articles.body: Give an agent a database tool and ask it about last quarter's revenue. Most of the time you get a good answer. Sometimes the tool comes back empty, or with something the agent doesn't quite understand, and the agent does what language models do best: it writes a plausible sentence with a plausible number in it. Nothing errors. The number just isn't real. This post builds a LangChain agent with one data tool that behaves differently. The tool returns either an answer with the query and rows behind it , or an explicit DECLINED , and the agent is told what to do with each. The data layer is FactQL , but the pattern (evidence in, declines out, a strict system prompt) works with any data tool you write. About 60 lines of Python, LangChain v1.

articles.title: SpaceX moves Starship Flight 15 booster to launch pad for 'squeeze test' ahead of epic double-catch attempt (photos)
articles.excerpt: SpaceX has moved its Starship Super Heavy booster to the pad to prep for the next test flight of the megarocket, a historic mission scheduled to launch this Friday (Nov. 13).
articles.body: SpaceX is one big step closer to the 15th test flight of its Starship megarocket. The company announced today (Nov. 10) that it had moved its latest Starship first stage, known as Super Heavy Booster 22, to the launch mount at its Starbase facility in South Texas ahead of Flight 15, which is scheduled to lift off this Friday (Nov. 13). During the upcoming launch test, SpaceX plans to catch both Booster 22 and Starship's Ship upper stage with its launch tower's "chopstick" arms in a double landing catch — something the private spaceflight company has never tried before. It will be the first full recovery of an orbital rocket in history. SpaceX's Flight 15 Starship Super Heavy booster in its assembly bay, before its move to Starbase's launch mount.

articles.title: Anthony Mackie, Ariana DeBose, and John Leguizamo reveal why they joined Andy Weir's sci-fi audio drama 'Exoplanet' (interview)
articles.excerpt: We hooked up with Mackie, DeBose, and Lequizamo to learn more about this renaissance of audio dramas and what attracted them to board Weir's sci-fi thriller.
articles.body: In any respectable audiobook project, finding the names of Andy Weir ("The Martian," "Project Hail Mary") and Benjamin Percy ("The Ninth Metal," "Wolverine") attached would elicit intense fan interest, but add the superstar vocal talents of Anthony Mackie ("Avengers: Infinity War," "Avengers: Doomsday"), Ariana DeBose ("West Side Story"), and John Leguizamo ("Ice Age"), and it catapults this sonic odyssey into the stratosphere. Such is the case with " Exoplanet ," Audible Original’s new 7-episode science fiction audio drama executive produced by Weir and penned by Percy. Its planet-hopping space disaster narrative sees the crew of the starship Wild Blue Yonder hit a quantum anomaly, forcing their ship to crash-land onto a deadly exoplanet.

articles.title: On this day in space! Nov. 10, 2013: Europe's GOCE satellite, the 'Ferrari of space,' fell out of orbit after mapping Earth's gravity field
articles.excerpt: On Nov. 10, 2013, Europe's GOCE satellite fell to Earth after four years in orbit mapping the planet's gravitational field. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Nov. 10, 2013, Europe's GOCE satellite fell to Earth after four years in orbit mapping the planet's gravitational field. GOCE, its name was short for Gravity field and steady-state Ocean Circulation Explorer, launched in 2009 on a mission to map Earth's gravity like never before. But despite that successful mission, it was doomed in 2013 when it ran out of fuel . At the time, controllers weren't sure where GOCE would fall back to Earth . Some people worried that it might crash into a populated area. However, the small spacecraft broke up in the atmosphere and didn't cause any property damage. It disintegrated about 50 miles above the Falkland Islands in the South Atlantic Ocean. The European Space Agency called the mission a success. GOCE lasted far longer than expected.
